checks.item: 1c. F-01: freeze write never skipped for an elapsed budget
checks.evidence: src/xverse/maestro/native/run_authority.c:163 calls write_freeze(e->cg,'1') with no time test; HEAD:162 was `if(now_ns()>=end||write_freeze(e->cg,'1'))`, which skipped the write once the budget had elapsed.

src/xverse/maestro/native/run_authority.c:166-174: the loop breaks on `!pending||now_ns()>=end` (172) and sleeps with poll(...,1) (173); every caller passes end <= min(generation, now+2 s): close_end 187 (CANCEL 399, rejection 525), lease expiry 506, cleanup 473-474.
checks.note: Bounded on the assumption that CLOCK_MONOTONIC works; see TPR-04 (pre-existing, identical in HEAD).

checks.item: 1e. F-01: independent close budget min(generation, now+2 s) on CANCEL and rejection path
checks.evidence: src/xverse/maestro/native/run_authority.c:187 close_end; used at 399 (CANCEL, replaces g->deadline) and 525 (rejection, replaces `until`). Same formula as cleanup() 473.
checks.note: When now_ns() returns 0, close_end returns generation, as cleanup() does (pre-existing pattern).

checks.item: 1f. F01R-02: all writes before any wait
checks.evidence: src/xverse/maestro/native/run_authority.c:159-165 issue every write and build `pending`; no poll or wait occurs before line 166. A slow unit therefore no longer delays later units' writes.

checks.item: 1g. F01R-02: each pending unit checked at least once
checks.evidence: src/xverse/maestro/native/run_authority.c:167-171 reads cgroup.events for every pending bit before the exit test at 172, so even with an already-elapsed `end` every pending unit is read once.
checks.note: Units whose write failed are not pending and are not read (see TPR-03); this matches the wording 'each pending unit' in finding 397.

checks.evidence: src/xverse/maestro/native/run_authority.c:175 `if(pending)g->freeze_failed=1;`; write failures set it at 163.

checks.item: 2a. Bit arithmetic for up to 16 units
checks.evidence: count is 1..16 (initialize, src/xverse/maestro/native/run_authority.c:288) and units[16] (53); all shifts are UINT64_C(1)<<i with i<16; pending&=~bit (170) clears only bit i. mask and pending are disjoint; mask < 1<<count.

src/xverse/maestro/native/run_authority.c:160 skips them before any dereference of history[0].cg (=-1 for unregistered units, set in main 501); they never enter `pending`, so the second pass never touches them. Not reported in the mask and do not set freeze_failed, as in HEAD.

src/xverse/maestro/native/run_authority.c:162 sets the mask bit and skips the write, as in HEAD:160. A generation removed after its write (between pass 1 and pass 2) makes field() fail and stays pending until `end`, then sets freeze_failed (TPR-02).

src/xverse/maestro/native/run_authority.c:170: a failing field() leaves the bit pending; it is re-read every iteration until `end`; if never confirmed, 175 sets freeze_failed and the bit stays out of the mask. Same outcome as HEAD's per-unit loop.

src/xverse/maestro/native/run_authority.c:166-174 cannot return before one full read pass and exits on !pending or now>=end. It cannot spin forever while the monotonic clock works; if now_ns() returns 0 permanently and a unit never reports frozen==1, `0>=end` is false and the loop does not terminate.
checks.note: Identical to HEAD's `while(now_ns()<end)` (F01R-08); recorded as TPR-04.

checks.evidence: src/xverse/maestro/native/run_authority.c:173 polls g->parent (pidfd of the parent) for POLLIN with a 1 ms timeout, as HEAD:166. Once the parent has exited, the pidfd is readable and poll returns immediately, so the wait busy-spins (up to 16 openat/read per iteration) until `end` (at most 2 s).
checks.note: Pre-existing and bounded; recorded under TPR-04.

checks.item: 2g. Returned mask meaning and client expectations
checks.evidence: Bit i is set iff unit i's current generation was removed (src/xverse/maestro/native/run_authority.c:162) or frozen==1 was observed during this call (170), the same predicate as HEAD:160,169-170. For the same kernel timing the new mask is a superset of HEAD's, because units reached after an elapsed budget are now read. affa_client.py:303 requires state < 1<<len(units) and reason in (5,6): run_reply (400) sends exactly the mask and CANCEL_REASON(5)/FREEZE_FAILED(6); affa_protocol.py:86 bounds state to 0..65535, which a 16-bit mask satisfies.

src/xverse/maestro/native/run_authority.c:399-400: only the budget changes (g->deadline -> close_end). run_broker.py:886 sends CANCEL with until <= now+1 s, so the helper may now reply after the client's receive deadline (F01R-01, recorded as deliberate in finding 396); the client then revokes instead of recording CANCELLED. No wire change.
checks.note: The two-pass loop reduces the time per close (one shared wait) relative to the intermediate version.

checks.evidence: src/xverse/maestro/native/run_authority.c:525: budget `until` -> close_end; reason PROTOCOL(4) -> FREEZE_FAILED(6) when g->freeze_failed. HEAD could wait up to `until` (<= receipt+5 s); the new budget is at most 2 s from the rejection, which can be shorter. Because writes are unconditional and the reply state stays 0, this does not weaken containment. The reason is taken from the sticky g->freeze_failed (TPR-01). affa_client.py:288-289 does not read the REJECTED reason.
checks.note: No behavioural regression for the client.

checks.evidence: src/xverse/maestro/native/run_authority.c:506 unchanged; it already passed min(generation, now+2 s) and now gets the two-pass behaviour.
checks.note: Uses `now` from the top of the loop iteration (F01R-08, pre-existing).

checks.evidence: src/xverse/maestro/native/run_authority.c:473-474 unchanged; close_authority shares `end` with the reap wait (488). As in HEAD, a unit that never reports frozen consumes the budget and leaves the reap wait no time, so cleanup returns 70; with the two-pass loop the consumption is one shared wait rather than per unit.

(a) matches 163, 166-175, 187, 399, 525; REJECTED keeps state 0 (525) and reason in 1..7. The '1..7 ... affa_protocol.py:108' wording was corrected in finding 396 (bound at affa_protocol.py:87; 108 requires a nonzero reason and state 0).

checks.item: 4b. Finding 395: REJECTED reason FREEZE_FAILED(6) when the refreeze is unconfirmed
checks.evidence: src/xverse/maestro/native/run_authority.c:525 selects 6 from g->freeze_failed, which is set at 163/175 and never cleared (src/xverse/maestro/native/run_authority.c:51,163,175 are the only writers). Reason 6 therefore means 'some freeze in this authority's life was unconfirmed', not only 'this refreeze was unconfirmed'.

checks.evidence: Two-pass structure, unconditional writes, at-least-once check of pending units and freeze_failed for still-pending units all match src/xverse/maestro/native/run_authority.c:155-177; numstat 18/10 against HEAD and binary 17f2476a2d41...c4af5 reproduced; the control's docstring states that the reason-6 and bounded-wait branches are not reached.

F-07: the only '0' writer is RELEASE (src/xverse/maestro/native/run_authority.c:443), gated by enabled() (106 requires !closed); the authority stays alive after CANCEL; bootstrap.py:848-860 _service_terminal requires a CANCELLED receipt or observed authority death. findings.title: freeze_failed is sticky, so reason 6 reports any earlier unconfirmed freeze, not only the current refreeze
findings.scenario: A close that times out (for example on lease expiry at 506, or a REJECTED refreeze) sets g->freeze_failed, which nothing clears. Every later REJECTED then carries reason 6 even if its own refreeze is fully confirmed, and a later CANCEL can return a complete mask together with reason 6, which run_broker.py:902 maps to ML-RUN-FREEZE-UNRESOLVED. Findings 395/397 describe reason 6 as 'when the refreeze could not be confirmed within the close budget'. The direction is conservative and affa_client.py does not read the REJECTED reason, so no containment property is weakened.
findings.recommendation: Either record in the review log that reason 6 (on REJECTED and CANCELLED) and cleanup's exit 70 reflect a sticky, authority-lifetime freeze failure, or have freeze_all report a per-call failure for the reply reason while keeping the sticky flag for cleanup(). Do not clear the sticky flag without a recorded rationale.

findings.title: A generation removed after its freeze write stays pending, consumes the budget and is reported unfrozen
findings.scenario: Pass 1 treats a removed current generation as covered (mask bit). If the cgroup is removed between the write and the read, field() fails with ENOENT on every read, the unit stays pending until `end` (up to 2 s), freeze_failed is set and the bit stays out of the mask. HEAD behaves the same. Conservative (under-reports), but spends the shared budget that cleanup() also uses for its reap wait.
findings.recommendation: Optional: when field() fails in the wait loop, test removed(e) and, if true, set the mask bit and clear the pending bit; otherwise record the conservative behaviour.

findings.title: Units whose freeze write fails are never read or retried
findings.scenario: write_freeze returning -1 (transient error) or 1 (ENOENT/ENODEV) sets freeze_failed and excludes the unit from `pending`, so a unit that is in fact frozen (for example by an earlier stop_child at 363) is not confirmed and its bit is missing from the mask. Same as HEAD; conservative. The 'checked at least once' guarantee of finding 397 applies to pending units only, which matches its wording.
findings.recommendation: Optional: read cgroup.events once for write-failed units too (or retry the write inside the wait loop) and keep freeze_failed for them; or keep as is and note it alongside F01R-06.

findings.title: Pre-existing: the wait is unbounded if the monotonic clock fails, and busy-spins when the parent has exited
findings.scenario: now_ns() returns 0 on clock_gettime failure; then `now_ns()>=end` is never true and, if a unit never reports frozen==1, the loop never ends (close_end and cleanup also fall back to end=generation when now is 0). If the parent has exited, poll on its pidfd returns immediately and the wait busy-spins until `end`. Both are identical in HEAD (F01R-08) and are not introduced by this diff.
findings.recommendation: Optional hardening: treat now_ns()==0 as budget exhausted in the exit test at 172; consider a sleep that does not depend on g->parent (e.g. poll(NULL,0,1)) when the parent pidfd is already readable.

findings.title: Rejection-path wait can be shorter than in HEAD
findings.scenario: HEAD waited for frozen==1 until the request's `until` (up to receipt+5 s); the new budget is at most now+2 s from the rejection. A refreeze that completes between 2 s and `until` is now reported as reason 6 where HEAD reported 4. The write itself is unconditional, so the boundary is still frozen by the kernel; only the confirmation and the reason differ.
findings.recommendation: None required; mention in the review log that the rejection-path confirmation window is capped at 2 s.

findings.title: Close-budget formula is written three times
findings.scenario: close_end (187), cleanup (473) and the lease-expiry call (506, with the loop-top `now`) compute the same min(generation, now+2 s) independently. They agree today; divergence in a later edit would silently change one close path.
findings.recommendation: Optional: call close_end(g) from cleanup() and the lease-expiry path.

verdict_rationale: Every live generation's cgroup.freeze write is issued before any wait and regardless of budget (163); one bounded wait reads each pending unit at least once (166-174); still-pending units set freeze_failed (175); CANCEL and the rejection path use close_end = min(generation, now+2 s) (187, 399, 525). The returned mask keeps HEAD's meaning and satisfies affa_client.py:303. No regression on CANCEL, rejection, lease-expiry or cleanup paths beyond the recorded F01R-01 timing trade-off. Residual items are one LOW (sticky reason-6 semantics versus the wording of findings 395/397) and NOTEs, all conservative in direction.
limits: Source reading and a warning-check build only; no execution, no kernel-level timing measurement, no test run. Supervisor-side freezing (F01R-03 rationale) was checked at source-reading level only.
